summary: Jessica Patey specializes in Indology and religious studies. She is a PhD candidate studying and holding a post at Harvard University (attested 2026).

Jessica X. Zu works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned PhDs from Pennsylvania State University (1997–2003) and Princeton University (2013–2020), and held an Associate Professor position at the University of Southern California in 2026.

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After degrees from SOAS, Panthéon-Sorbonne, École du Louvre, and Paris-Sorbonne/Sorbonne University, she held postdoctoral, Junior Professor, and Professor posts at Ruhr University Bochum.

Jesung Woo specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Woo earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1995) and held posts at Hiroshima University (1997–1998) and Dongguk University (2001–2003).
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Flick studied under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. A disciple of Weijue Shi, Deng succeeded him in 2005.

Jian Ouyang (1871–1943) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Renshan Yang from circa 1904 to 1911 and founded and headed the China Institute of Inner Learning (~1922–1943).

Jiang Wu works in Buddhist studies and sinology. After studying at Nankai University and Harvard University under Tu Weiming, Robert M. Gimello, Peter K. Bol, and Zhichao Chen, Wu served as Professor at the University of Arizona.
Jianming Hu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a researcher position at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang (1895–1959) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. Wang was a disciple of Gongga Rinpoche and is attested as a PhD student at Columbia University.

Jiayao An specializes in archaeology and sinology. An studied under Su Bai (~1978–1981) and joined the Institute of Archaeology at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences around 1981 as a special researcher and Xi'an research office director.

Jiayue Kang works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. After graduate studies at East China Normal University and an MA in Sanskrit at Silpakorn University (2022–2025), Kang held a post at Silpakorn University.

Jiegang Gu (1893–1980) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Peking University under Hu Shih and Taiyan Zhang, later holding posts at Peking University, Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.
Jien Abe (1937–2001) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Abe completed graduate studies at the University of Tokyo and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. After studying at Tunghai University (~1965–1969), Lan served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from circa 1985 until retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya (1929–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington (~1960–1963).

Jigme Chhoeda works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under several traditional teachers, later serving as Abbot of Tango Monastery and holding Lopen posts in the Central Monastic Body and Dratshang Lhentshog.
Jigme Pema Wangchen works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Dzi Gar Khenpo Nor Yang, Drukpa Khenpo Ngawang Chödrak, and Mi-pham-bśad-sgrub-chos-kyi-ñin-byed-mchog.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu specializes in Buddhist studies. Junu earned an MA from Fo Guang University under supervisor Yongdong Shi and studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian (attested 2013).
